articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the February 1995 issue (Volume 6, Number 2) of "SJAA EPHEMERIS," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It provides a snapshot of the club's activities and astronomical information from that specific period.

articles.title: The Eyepiece
articles.summary: This article from "The Eyepiece" newsletter announces the upcoming San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) Board of Directors election, with six candidates running for five seats. It also details the resignations of two board members, Gene Cisneros and Jack Zeiders, and the interim appointments of Rich Newschaefer and Lew Kurtz. Additionally, the document provides a comprehensive calendar of SJAA activities for February and March, including star parties, general meetings with speakers, and observational astronomy classes.

articles.title: Forty Years Ago This Month
articles.summary: This article, commemorating a 40-year anniversary, details a pivotal meeting from four decades prior, outlining the early planning and a subsequent club gathering. The February 21st meeting featured talks on constellation Gemini, Jupiter's moons and phenomena, astronomical measurement methods like parallax and parsecs, and practical advice for amateur telescope users. It serves as a historical look back at the origins and early activities of the astronomy club.

articles.title: ECLIPSE OVER THE ALTIPLANO
articles.summary: Ernie Piini chronicles his expedition to Bolivia with his daughter to witness a total solar eclipse over the Altiplano. The journey combined cultural immersion at Lake Titicaca and Tiwanaku Ruins with observations of the Southern Skies, alongside meticulous preparations for the main celestial event. Despite concerns about cloud cover, challenges like altitude sickness, and technical preparations, the expedition successfully viewed a vibrant and awe-inspiring total solar eclipse, marked by a significant temperature drop and the visible "Diamond Ring" and corona.

articles.title: THE ALTIPLANO
articles.summary: This article describes a post-eclipse travel experience in Bolivia, detailing a visit to La Paz, including the Hotel El Presidente, the Witch Doctor's Market, and Moon Valley, likened to Bryce Canyon. The author also reflects on their eclipse photography success and interprets a coca tea leaf reading regarding their camera experiments and the overall trip outcome.

articles.title: The Lunatic Fringe
articles.summary: This article, 'The Lunatic Fringe,' provides a guide for observing specific lunar features when the Moon is about 9 days old and near the terminator, even when its brightness makes fainter objects difficult to see. It lists objects by difficulty (Easy, Medium, Challenge) including prominent craters like Copernicus and Eratosthenes, the flooded crater Stadius, and challenging lunar domes near Hortensius. The author also recommends 'Atlas of the Moon' by Antonin Rukl as a helpful resource for lunar observation.

articles.title: STAR TESTING ASTRONOMICAL TELESCOPES
articles.summary: This article is a review of Harold Richard Suiter's book, "STAR TESTING ASTRONOMICAL TELESCOPES," published by Willmann-Bell. The book provides a comprehensive guide to evaluating telescope optics through star testing, detailing various optical problems and other testing methods like Foucault and Interferometry. It is highly recommended for both average telescope users and technically inclined individuals seeking a detailed reference.

articles.title: SL-9 Impacts on Jupiter
articles.summary: A team of four scientists and engineers from Lockheed Missiles and Space Company presented their successful endeavor to observe the SL-9 impacts on Jupiter using amateur telescopes and video recording equipment. Operating from White Mountain at 10,000 ft, they overcame challenging conditions to record continuous video of the impacts. Through post-processing and image enhancement, they obtained high-quality images comparable to those from much larger observatory telescopes.

articles.title: Impacts
articles.summary: This article highlights the significant role of image processing for amateur astronomers, especially for capturing unique transitory events like planetary impacts. It emphasizes that this technique, which allows for real-time recording and post-processing, is tolerant of issues like vibration and tracking jitter. The method opens up new possibilities for amateurs, even those using Dobsonian telescopes without sophisticated tracking systems.

articles.title: Board of Director Candidates
articles.summary: The article introduces candidates for the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) Board of Directors, urging members to cast their votes at the upcoming February general meeting. It provides brief biographies and statements from most candidates, highlighting their experience, interests in amateur astronomy, and perspectives on club priorities like educational outreach, financial stability, insurance, and internet access.

articles.title: News and Views
articles.summary: This 'News and Views' section describes an observatory centered around a large Treppower refractor, complemented by various smaller Zeiss refractors and Cassegrain reflectors. It also includes a personal message from Bob Brauer wishing a Happy New Year and inviting participation in upcoming SJAA elections, providing contact information. The content is dated February 1995.

articles.title: New Telescope Donated by Paul Barton
articles.summary: On January 7, 1995, Ken Miura donated a new 60mm Bushnell refractor telescope to the SJAA Telescope Loan Program, implicitly on behalf of Paul Barton. This portable unit, valued at approximately $450, is in excellent condition and includes all accessories, making it a valuable addition for club members. The article expresses gratitude for the generous contribution.

articles.title: News and Views by SJAA President Bob Brauer
articles.summary: The article recounts SJAA President Bob Brauer's business trip to Berlin, where he dedicated a free day to exploring the city's astronomical attractions. He visited the impressive Zeiss Grossplanetarium, noting its massive size, before discovering and touring the historic Archenhold Observatory. Brauer was particularly amazed by the Treptower Refractor, a huge and historically significant instrument still in use despite its exposure to the elements.

articles.title: December 21, 1994
articles.summary: This document features a letter from long-time member Dick Barrett, dated December 21, 1994, recounting his recollections about the San Jose astronomical society's founding, his work covering Lick Observatory, and a memoir he is writing. He shares personal anecdotes, including his experience with Halley's Comet and mentions several notable astronomers and club members. The document also includes a calendar of 1994 events for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA).

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Status
articles.summary: This document provides an update on the status of telescopes available for loan through a program, detailing which telescopes are currently borrowed, their due dates, and which are available. It also notes a solar telescope available for experienced members and provides instructions for interested individuals to borrow a telescope by contacting Paul Barton.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: The 'ASTRO ADS' section offers free classified advertisements for noncommercial sellers of astronomically related products or services. Ads run for approximately three months and must be submitted to the editor by the 12th of each month. Current listings include various used telescopes and components, such as Celestron C-5 and Ultima 8-inch models, Meade 6-inch OTA, Questar 3.5-inch, mirrors, and accessories.

articles.title: Long-time SJAA member
articles.summary: Doug Wells, a long-time SJAA member, is seeking a ride to the general meetings as he no longer drives. He lives at Villa Fontana on Prospect Road, and interested members are asked to call him at 255-5555 apartment 227 to arrange transportation.

articles.title: Lunar Phases: Date Rise Trans Set
articles.summary: This document provides a listing of lunar phases for the current month, including their dates, rise times, transit times, and set times. It details information for the First Quarter, Full Moon, and Last Quarter, noting the absence of a New Moon for the specified period.

articles.title: NEARER PLANETS:
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical data for the 'Nearer Planets' (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn) for three specific dates (07, 17, 27 of an unspecified month). It lists their distances in Astronomical Units (A.U.), magnitudes, and what appear to be rise, transit, and set times. Additionally, it includes similar data for the Sun (SOL), detailing its star type, magnitude, right ascension, declination, and corresponding times.

articles.title: ASTRONOMICAL TWILIGHT:
articles.summary: This document provides a tabular list of Julian Dates (JD) along with their corresponding start and end times for astronomical twilight. It details specific twilight periods across several dates, beginning with JD 2,449,755 and continuing for subsequent dates like JD 2,449,765 and JD 2,449,775. The data indicates the precise window during which astronomical twilight occurs.

articles.title: SIDEREAL TIME:
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical timing data for Saturday, February 25, 1995, in Pacific Standard Time. It includes sidereal time transits, local midnight, sunset, twilight end, moon rise/set times, and calculates total astrophotography hours. The data's derivation is attributed to specific astronomy software and a book on personal computer astronomy.

articles.title: Offices and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current offices and board of directors, including the President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, and several Directors. For most individuals, their name and a contact phone number are provided.

articles.title: Ephemeris Contributors
articles.summary: This document lists individuals contributing to, editing, and distributing an ephemeris. It provides contact names and phone numbers for Don Machholz, Paul Barton, Rich Stanton, and Bob Madden, detailing their roles in the publication process.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: This article, 'COMET COMMENTS' by Don Machholz, reports on recent discoveries and recoveries of faint comets, including updates on Periodic Comet Borrelly, McNaught-Russell, Wild 4, and Schwassmann-Wachmann 3. It primarily details upcoming changes by the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory's Central Bureau for Astronomical Telegrams regarding preliminary designations and proper naming conventions for comets, aiming to standardize and simplify the process. The new system will use year, half-month, and discovery order, alongside new rules for assigning proper names.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for Periodic Comet 19P/BORRELLY, detailing its predicted celestial coordinates (Right Ascension, Declination), elongation, and sky magnitude for dates spanning from January 23 to March 9, 1995. It also lists the comet's key orbital elements, including its perihelion date, distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period.

articles.title: EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: EPHEMERIS is a monthly publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association, providing guidelines for members to submit articles. Submissions, preferably typed or on diskette, are due by the 12th of the previous month and should be sent to the editor, Bob Madden.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers various membership options, including individual, membership with Sky & Telescope, and junior memberships, with corresponding fees. Prospective members can join by submitting a form with payment to the treasurer or bringing it to an SJAA meeting, and general contact and information hotline details are provided.
